text: Keep Aimparency's code-execution surface in the hands of its operator
description: Felix 2026-11-01: through the wrapper feature, an ordinary Aimparency instance is a gate to a terminal, i.e. code execution and full control of the machine. Every server that can start agents, loops or clones (backend, broker, agent sessions) must answer only its operator: loopback by default, explicit opt-in for a network interface, no driving from foreign web pages. Felix 2026-11-02: on a hosted instance (behind nginx) the operator role is admin, with no separate role: only admins get the wrapped-agent shell, and creating an admin warns that this is shell access as the aimparency user (/etc, every env secret). Read and write accounts never get it.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Closes the two widest doors (LAN exposure and drive-by websites) without breaking the UI, MCP, mobile via adb reverse, or dev:host.
A server that only follows git can be shown to anyone without widening the code-execution surface.
supportingConnections.reflection: Held by construction: the sync only fetches and fast-forwards, so a hosted server stays a follower of git with no new capability.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: People hand out admin carefully once every path that creates one says plainly that it is an SSH-equivalent login.
One credential checked at every hop keeps the shell with the people the operator made admin, even with the server reachable from the internet.
supportingConnections.reflection: Held in tests: the gateway checks the admin cookie and origin at the only exposed hop, and broker and sessions are loopback-only. A demoted or logged-out admin is refused on the next request; an already open terminal socket stays open until it closes.

status.comment: All parts done: session sockets (0f307c81), backend/broker loopback + origin gate (de7abc26), hosted git following (b008055a), admin-shell warning (266dcf6b), admin-only hosted shell behind the one port, opt-in via AIMPARENCY_AGENTS (69a7ab7c). Remaining exposure by design: pnpm dev:host opens the dev stack to the named interface (tailnet) without a login; anyone who can reach it from a non-browser client can drive it.
